name: South Korea

income_tax.summary: Progressive income tax of 6% to 45% plus local income tax of 10% of the tax gives a top combined marginal rate of 49.5%. Foreign employees who start work in Korea by 31 December 2026 can elect a flat 19% (20.9% with local tax) for up to 20 years in place of progressive rates and deductions; a 21% rate and 2029 deadline are only proposed. Employees pay about 9.7% in pension, health, long-term care and employment insurance.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Self-employed people are 'local subscribers': they pay the full National Pension (9.5% total rate in 2026, no employer share; PwC) and regional health insurance. The NHIS page gives a 2026 health insurance rate of 7.19%, and long-term care is 13.14% of the health premium (braindetox.kr), which matches PwC's roughly 8.135% for health plus long-term care. The 17.63% used (9.5% + 7.19% x 1.1314) is therefore built from sourced rates but is an upper-bound ESTIMATE: regional premiums are also assessed on property points, and the pension is capped at the same KRW 6,590,000 monthly income ceiling (about KRW 79m a year), neither of which is modelled.
income_tax.local_tax_note: Marginal rates shown already include local income tax of 10% of the tax (PwC, reviewed 2 July 2026). personal_allowance is the basic personal deduction of KRW 1.5 million for the taxpayer (PwC deductions page); the employment income deduction (70% of the first KRW 5m, 40% to KRW 15m, 15% to KRW 45m, 5% to KRW 100m, 2% above; capped at KRW 20m; employees only) and the insurance deductions are not included. Employee contributions: National Pension 4.75% on monthly pay up to KRW 6,590,000 (from July 2026; maximum KRW 313,025 a month), health insurance including long-term care about 4.0674% (monthly cap KRW 10,390,220 in total), employment insurance 0.90%. The pension cap means the 9.7174% total overstates contributions at high pay; no single cap is recorded.

sources.title: Korea, Republic of - Taxes on personal income

open_questions: Self-employed rate is a composite of sourced component rates; the exact regional (local subscriber) income-point formula and the property component were not found.
Employment income deduction and tax credits are not modelled (only the KRW 1.5m basic deduction).
Pension ceiling KRW 6,590,000 (PwC, July 2026) vs KRW 6,370,000 (secondary guide): PwC used.

employment_deduction.note: Earned income deduction: 70% of pay to KRW 5M; 40% of the excess to 15M; 15% to 45M; 5% to 100M; 2% above; capped at KRW 20M.

open_questions: Proposal to move to 21% from 2027 and extend to 2029 was not enacted as of the source.
Local income tax (10% of the tax) is on top of the 19%.
regimes.name: 19% flat tax for foreign employees
regimes.description: Foreign employees who start work in Korea no later than 31 December 2026 may elect a flat 19% rate (excluding 10% local tax, so 20.9%) on employment income instead of progressive 6-45%. Electing forfeits other deductions, exemptions and credits; not available when working for a related-party company. Lasts 20 years from first day of work.
regimes.duration_note: 20 years from the first day of work in Korea through the end of the tax year before the 20-year anniversary. A reform proposal of 3 August 2026 would raise the rate to 21% (23.1% with local tax) and extend the sunset to 31 December 2029 from 1 January 2027; not enacted.

sources.title: Korea, Republic of - Individual income determination (19% flat rate)
KPMG Flash Alert 2026-235: Korea 2026 tax reform proposal

open_questions: Threshold is the 2023 figure (KRW 85m, twice the prior year's GNI per capita) on the consulate page; the current-year GNI-based figure was not found.

Foreign-source income of a resident visitor: PwC says residents with five years or less in the last ten are taxed on Korea-source income, and foreign-source income only if paid by a Korean entity or transferred to Korea; whether a nomad's pay for work done in Korea counts as Korea-source was not found, so treatment stays standard.
regimes.name: Workation visa (F-1-D)
regimes.description: One-year visa for people who work remotely for a foreign company, with annual income of twice Korea's prior-year GNI per capita (about KRW 85m per the 2024 consulate page), one year of experience in the same industry, age 18+ and KRW 100m medical and repatriation insurance. Local employment is restricted.
regimes.duration_note: Valid one year, one extension of one year possible in Korea.

costs.notes: Seoulstart figures are 'typical ranges' with no sample size. Monthly rent is paid on top of a large refundable deposit; jeonse (lump-sum deposit) is an alternative.

residence_routes: EU, US and other citizens: remote workers can use the F-1-D workation visa (foreign employer or own foreign company, income about KRW 85m, 1+1 years). Skilled employees need an employer-sponsored work visa (E-series); specific categories were not verified on an opened official page. The 19% flat tax is open to foreign employees of any nationality who start work by 31 December 2026.
open_questions: Official Ministry of Justice / HiKorea pages not opened.
